title: House and Visitor
premise: Jude Vane, a property surveyor, arrives at Hollowmere House to appraise it for its dying owner, Marguerite Ashe, and discovers the house reflects rooms one second late in every mirror—as if something is copying the house and getting better at it. Jude realizes the 'visitor' was invited decades ago by a previous resident's desperate bargain, and that the appraisal itself is the ritual: whoever signs the papers becomes the house's next keeper. As the night stretches toward sunrise, Jude must choose between fleeing (and letting the visitor follow him home through his own reflection) or signing and surrendering his memories of everyone he loves. He signs—but writes his own name backwards, corrupting the contract, trapping the visitor in a house that now reflects nothing at all.
about_author: Emrys Fairweather is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent fifteen years cataloguing structural decay in Victorian houses across the English countryside. They write horror about places that remember more than the people who live in them.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Jude Vane accepts an unusually lucrative appraisal job at Hollowmere House, noting the seller's odd condition: he must stay until sunrise to complete the survey. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a low hum of unease—he needs this money, and he doesn't ask why.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: Jude's childhood in a house with noises he learned to rationalize—pipes, settling wood, wind. His mother's disappearance taught him that not asking questions was survival. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: we learn invisibility is his oldest coping strategy.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Jude arrives at dusk. The house is immaculate but wrong—dustless, warm, expectant. Marguerite Ashe, frail and sharp-tongued, greets him and says only: 'Don't mind the mirrors.' POV: Jude. Emotional beat: dread dressed as hospitality; the reader feels watched before Jude does.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Jude begins his survey, cataloguing rooms with clinical precision as armor against the house's stillness. Every room contains exactly one mirror, each covered. He uncovers one out of habit—and sees the room behind him, empty, where he is standing. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the first crack in his rationalism.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Testing the mirror, Jude confirms it: reflections lag by exactly one second. Worse, the reflected room sometimes holds furniture the real room lacks. He tells himself it's a trick of old glass. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: denial curdling into obsession—he can't stop looking.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Terms
chapters.summary: Marguerite serves tea and explains the sale must close at dawn, no earlier, no later. She watches Jude with pity. When he asks about the mirrors she says, 'They're not broken. They're learning.' POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the horror shifts from the house to the people who know about it.

chapters.title: The Previous Residents
chapters.summary: In the study, Jude finds appraisal documents going back to 1893—each signed at dawn, each surveyor's name struck through afterward. The last entry before Marguerite's is half-finished. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: pattern recognition as terror; he is part of a sequence.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: A hidden letter reveals the origin: in 1893, a grieving owner summoned something to fill her empty house, and it came—but it needed a keeper bound by signature, renewed every generation. Marguerite is the current keeper, dying. POV: Jude (reading). Emotional beat: grief as the door horror walks through.

chapters.title: The Copying Room
chapters.summary: Jude returns to the hall mirror and finds the reflected hallway now contains a figure standing where he stood a second ago. It isn't mimicking him anymore. It's rehearsing him. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: from observation to pursuit—the lag is closing.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: At midnight Jude tries to leave; the front door opens onto the same hallway behind him. Windows show the house's interior, not the night. Marguerite, unbothered: 'It wants you to finish the survey.' POV: Jude. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; escape reframed as complicity.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite admits she has kept the visitor fed for forty years with her memories—she no longer remembers her husband's face. Signing the papers transfers the burden. She begs Jude to take it. POV: alternating Jude/Marguerite. Emotional beat: sympathy weaponized; survival has always had a price here.

chapters.title: The Price Itemized
chapters.summary: Jude studies the contract: the keeper keeps the house and their life, but surrenders their memories annually—starting with the ones they love most. He thinks of his mother, of the noises they survived together. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit—what would you pay to keep existing?

chapters.title: Reflections Without Him
chapters.summary: The mirrors now reflect rooms Jude isn't in, furnished with his own apartment, his own life—rehearsed perfectly. The lag is gone. The copy is ready to replace him if he runs. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: invisibility fails; the house has seen him completely.

chapters.title: His Mother's House
chapters.summary: A memory-chapter: young Jude and his mother in the house with the noises. She sang to drown them out. One night she went quiet mid-song. He never asked what she traded. POV: Jude (memory). Emotional beat: devastating implication—his whole childhood was a keeping.

chapters.title: The Strike-Through Names
chapters.summary: Jude deciphers the ledger: every struck-through surveyor didn't die—they were erased, remembered by no one, absorbed as the house's staff. Their reflections still move in the mirrors, dusting rooms forever. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: horror of oblivion worse than death.

chapters.title: Negotiation at 4 A.M.
chapters.summary: Jude confronts the visitor directly through the great mirror, speaking aloud for the first time instead of staying invisible. He offers a counter-bargain. The reflection stops moving and listens. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed—the passive survivor chooses to act.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Marguerite weakens rapidly as dawn nears; the house grows hungry, walls breathing, mirrors multiplying down corridors that shouldn't exist. Jude has minutes to decide. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: climax pressure—every option costs everything.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Jude signs the papers at first light—but writes his name mirrored, backwards, the way he'd practiced all night. The contract accepts it and chokes on it: a keeper who is his own reflection cannot be copied or erased. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: triumph through self-knowledge; the trick was being both himself and his reflection.

chapters.title: What the House Reflected
chapters.summary: The visitor, bound to a contract it cannot parse, collapses inward. The mirrors go dark one by one—not broken, but reflecting nothing, because there is finally nothing left to copy. Marguerite dies smiling, remembering her husband's face at last. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: release and grief intertwined.

chapters.title: Appraisal Complete
chapters.summary: Jude finishes the survey honestly, noting every defect, and files it. The house is valued at nothing—uninsurable, unsellable—which means no one will ever be invited again. He pockets no fee. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: quiet moral resolution; some prices should end the market.

chapters.title: The Noise Next Door
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Jude hears familiar settling sounds in his own flat. Instead of explaining them away, he walks to the mirror and introduces himself. The reflection greets him on time. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: transformation—he no longer survives by not asking.

chapters.title: House and Visitor
chapters.summary: Final image: Hollowmere stands empty, its mirrors blank, while somewhere a new house learns its first delayed second. Jude keeps the backwards-signed page framed on his wall—a reminder that he was once a visitor too, and chose to stay visible. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: haunted peace; memory, even painful, is the price worth paying.
